trust_decision.summary: The referer is trusted only if it parses to a same-origin URL (scheme, host and port compared) or to a rooted relative path, and the assembled redirect target is then emitted as a Location; the published fix adds the missing condition that the assembled target must not start with '//' (a network-path reference the browser resolves to another host).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names a redirect target built from a '\u00a0//host\u00a0 path', so a reader looks at validatedRefererRedirect, where redirectTarget is assembled from refURL.EscapedPath() and returned to the caller for http.Redirect.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST to any app fragment route (e.g. POST /test/abc/frag), served through internal/server/router.go:158 -> App.ServeHTTP -> createHandlerFunc; the sink is http.Redirect at internal/app/handler.go:410
fix_sites.module_kind: internal HTTP handler (internal/app, app server runtime)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route: the only candidate in the tree is the upstream-Location rewriter at internal/app/setup.go:986, which a solver can dismiss because its input is the proxied app's own response, not a client-supplied value.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate behaviours sit next to the sink: (a) a same-origin referer must still produce a 303 to its escaped path with query and fragment preserved (/test/abc?q=1#frag), and (b) when a referer is rejected the route must fall through and render the full page with 200 rather than redirect (to '/' or anywhere else). An over-broad fix (rejecting any path containing '//', or redirecting to '/' on rejection) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: absolute same-origin referer whose path starts with '//' (http://example.com//evil.com) - caught because the assembled target starts with '//'
rooted-relative referer '//evil.com' (no scheme, no host, path passes the HasPrefix(path, "/") test) - caught by the same target check
same-origin referer with query and fragment, which still redirects with ?query and #fragment appended

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a referer-based Post/Redirect/Get redirect for starlark action POSTs, sharing validatedRefererRedirect
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Actions are the other POST mutation surface in the app runtime and already compute isHtmxRequest; a maintainer implementing PRG for actions would plausibly reuse the same helper, putting a second caller one package away in internal/app/action.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a '//' guard in rewriteProxyLocation so the rewritten Location honours the doc comment 'In both cases the returned Location is path-absolute'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The doc comment already asserts the exact invariant the advisory is about, in a second function that assembles a client-facing Location from a parsed URL path (setup.go:1006-1012); a maintainer hardening open redirects would reasonably guard both.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: same-origin validation of the url passed to ace.redirect / ace.response(redirect=...)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the app-level redirect API in the same function that already contains the referer guard, so it is the nearest place a maintainer would extend the check to.

O9_family: CWE-601 URL redirection to untrusted site (open redirect) via a path/authority parsing differential on a '//' prefixed relative reference

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26.3 (go.mod:6), standard 'go test ./internal/app/...'; no vendor directory, modules fetched once
O10_build.project_tests: internal/app/tests/fragment_test.go TestFragmentPostRedirect covers the fragment PRG referer cases (same-origin accepted, external rejected, non-rooted rejected) using an in-memory FS and httptest; internal/app/proxy_host_test.go TestRewriteProxyLocation covers the separate proxy Location rewriter.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the rejection inside the switch on the parsed referer (e.g. reject when refURL.Host != "", or check refURL.Path) instead of on the assembled redirect target, which still lets the rooted-relative reference '//evil.com' through.
